test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following sectors contribute the most to GDP in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tertiary sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **tertiary sector** is indeed the largest contributor to India’s GDP, as highlighted by several key points:
 
• The services sector accounts for **54.72%** of India's total Gross Value Added (GVA) of **267.62 lakh crore INR**, which amounts to approximately **146.44 lakh crore INR** in 2023-24.
 
• Historical data shows a shift in sector contributions: in 1950-51, agriculture dominated with **51.81%**, while services accounted for only **33.25%**. By 2013-14, the share of services had increased to **57.03%**, demonstrating a long-term trend of growth in this sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The industry sector contributes **27.62%** to the GVA, with a value of **73.93 lakh crore INR**, while the agriculture and allied sector has a share of **17.66%**.
 
• At 2011-12 prices, the composition of the sectors reflects a similar trend: services (54.61%), industry (30.87%), and agriculture & allied (14.52%), indicating a stable dominance of the tertiary sector.
 
• The estimated shares for the primary (19.62%), secondary (25.66%), and tertiary sectors (54.72%) illustrate the significant role of services in the Indian economy.
